title: Amos 7:10–17
context: Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, reports Amos to King Jeroboam as a conspirator and tells Amos to go back to Judah and prophesy there, since Bethel is the king’s sanctuary and a royal house. Amos answers that he was no prophet nor a prophet’s son, but a herdsman and a farmer of sycamore figs whom the LORD took from following the flock and sent to prophesy to Israel. He then announces the LORD’s word against Amaziah and repeats that Israel will go into captivity. Bethel had been a royal shrine since Jeroboam son of Nebat set up a golden calf there (1 Kings 12:28–29). Shared ground: both traditions read the scene as a clash between the LORD’s word and a religious establishment tied to royal power, and both see the prophet’s authority resting on the LORD’s call rather than on office or training.

verses.text: Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the middle of the house of Israel. The land is not able to bear all his words.
verses.arminianNotes: Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, Arminian readers see a religious leader treating the LORD’s word as political conspiracy and appealing to the king.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note Amaziah’s claim that the land is not able to bear all his words. The complaint unintentionally acknowledges the weight of the prophetic word.

verses.text: For Amos says, ‘Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.’ ”
verses.arminianNotes: For Amos says, ‘Jeroboam will die by the sword,’ Arminian readers note that Amaziah reports Amos’s words loosely, since 7:9 spoke of the house of Jeroboam rather than of the king himself.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers observe that the report of exile is accurate: Israel would be led away captive (2 Kings 17:6). The difference about Jeroboam is named without harmonizing it.

verses.text: Amaziah also said to Amos, “You seer, go, flee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there,
verses.arminianNotes: You seer, go, flee away into the land of Judah, Arminian readers see Amaziah trying to send Amos home, perhaps implying that prophecy is a trade to be practiced for bread.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the title seer need not be an insult, though Amaziah’s tone is dismissive. His command is to prophesy anywhere but in Israel.

verses.text: but don’t prophesy again any more at Bethel; for it is the king’s sanctuary, and it is a royal house!”
verses.arminianNotes: but don’t prophesy again any more at Bethel; Arminian readers see the claim that Bethel is the king’s sanctuary and a royal house, putting royal interest above the LORD’s word.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that Bethel had been a royal shrine since Jeroboam son of Nebat set up a calf there (1 Kings 12:29), and Amos 3:14 and 5:5 speak against it. Its exact site is commonly but tentatively identified.

verses.text: Then Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son, but I was a herdsman, and a farmer of sycamore figs;
verses.arminianNotes: Then Amos answered Amaziah, Arminian readers hear I was no prophet as Amos denying that he belonged to a professional class; his authority came from the LORD’s call, not from training.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the line can be read as past (as here) or as a present disclaimer, and a prophet’s son is commonly taken as a member of a prophetic group (compare 2 Kings 2:3). Both readings stress the LORD’s call.

verses.text: and the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to my people Israel.’
verses.arminianNotes: and the LORD took me from following the flock, Arminian readers see the LORD’s initiative in calling an ordinary man and sending him with a message to Israel.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the command, Go, prophesy to my people Israel. Shared ground: both traditions see the prophet’s commission as coming entirely from the LORD.

verses.text: Now therefore listen to the LORD’s word: ‘You say, Don’t prophesy against Israel, and don’t preach against the house of Isaac.’
verses.arminianNotes: Now therefore listen to the LORD’s word: Arminian readers see Amos turning Amaziah’s prohibition back on him, so that the one who forbade prophecy now hears a prophecy.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that Amaziah is quoted telling Amos not to preach against the house of Isaac. The LORD’s word cannot be silenced by human authority.

verses.text: Therefore the LORD says: ‘Your wife shall be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, and your land shall be divided by line; and you yourself shall die in a land that is unclean, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.’ ”
verses.arminianNotes: Therefore the LORD says: Arminian readers see judgment falling on Amaziah’s household and land, and on Amaziah himself, who will die in a land that is unclean, that is, in exile.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers read the verse soberly as the covenant curses of war and exile reaching the priest’s own family. The closing words repeat the announcement that Israel will go into captivity.
